text:
maya: Quick heads-up — I'm opening this thread to collect telemetry and action items from last night's FlashAttention v2/v3 canary. Found a few perf blips when paged-attn is enabled with KV warm starts. :eyes:
ben: saw it too. numbers?
maya: baseline qps per-GPU dropped ~12% for short-context workloads (seq<=128) on v3 kernel, but latency tail increased only on cold KV hits.
liam: interesting — so throughput drops but p99 only for cold cache? can you paste the profile?
maya: paste of trimmed profile: ```
# sample profile (truncated)
Kernel: flash_v3_fused
Seq: 64
Batches/sec: 980 -> 860
Avg latency/token: 2.3ms -> 2.9ms
KV cache miss ratio during ramp: 0.18
CPU glue time increase: +12ms
```
sophie: might be the page-alignment path in v3 that does extra memcpy on first use. we added a small allocator roundup for paged blocks.
alex: also saw higher mutex contention in kv-manager on host side during warmstart, likely from concurrent prefetch threads.
ben: reproduction steps?
maya: local repro command we used: ```
./run_canary.sh --model gpt-open-16k --kernel flash_v3_fused --profile --workload short_context --kv-mode paged
```
liam: can we try toggling the feature flag that disables the paged-alignment optimization? i.e. ff:attn_paged_align:false
sophie: I can push a debug flag build to the canary pool to compare. prepping a build now.
ops-bot: deploy queued: canary-pool-7 -> image:attn-debug-2026-03-18-02 (:rocket:)
ben: while we're here, check batching heuristics — v3's continuous batching increase may be stealing cycles from small requests. maybe auto-batch-size clamp needs lowering for seq<=128.
maya: agree. current heuristic: auto_batch_size = min(128, floor(512/seq_len)). For seq 64 that gives 8 -> too big?
liam: math seems off for peak-CPU utilization. what if we change to: auto_batch_size = clamp(2, 32, floor(256/seq_len)) for v3 only?
alex: run a quick A/B in canary: half hosts with old heuristic, half with new. measure tokens/sec and p99.
sophie: pushed canary with both variants and added a trace tag: "attn_variant=kv_bench_v3_a" / "_v3_b". collecting 30m of traces.
maya: FYI, telemetry added: kv_miss, kv_eviction_rate, batch_size, kernel_name, seq_len, cpu_glue_ms, cuda_kernel_ms.
ben: any perf regressions beyond throughput? e.g., increased memory for paging or higher GPU SM occupancy causing stalls?
liam: preliminary flamegraph shows a spike in host-side `kv_prefetch_worker` and in `cudaMemcpyAsync` for first token of each sequence — matches the cold KV hypothesis.
alex: we should also test fallback path: when flash_v3_fused fails, route to flash_v2_unfused and compare quality/cost. add a canary rule: fallback_ratio=0.05 for 24h.
maya: I'll add a rollout checklist: 
- hold: stop full prod expansion until 24h canary completes
- telemetry: ensure p50/p90/p99, tokens/sec, kv_miss, batch_size exported
- flags: ff:attn_kernel=auto (default), ff:attn_v3_enable=true, ff:attn_paged_align=true/false for A/B
- fallback: attn_fallback_kernel=flash_v2_unfused, ratio=5%
- alerting: p99 latency +20% OR tokens/sec -10% -> paged-attn rollback
- ops playbook entry: `./scripts/rollout/attn_rollback.sh <pool>`
ben: good checklist. add note: quantized kernels behave differently; include quantization profile in canary.
sophie: can we gate the v3 optimizer by sequence length? e.g., enable for seq>256 only initially. that might avoid short-seq regressions.
liam: yes, add routing rule: if seq_len <= 128 -> prefer flash_v2_unfused, else allow v3. we can implement as routing policy expression.
maya: experiment snapshot will be saved at 3309874000. if canary looks good, plan a staggered ramp: 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with automated rollback on alerts.
alex: one more: KV eviction cadence seems aggressive under the new allocator due to smaller page chunks. bump eviction window from 60s -> 120s for v3 hosts in canary.
ben: noted. who owns follow-ups?
maya: owners: maya (overall), ben (batching heuristics), sophie (canary builds/telemetry), liam (routing rules/fallback), alex (kv manager changes).
ops-bot: canary job finished: results uploaded -> https://telemetry.internal/reports/3309873210 (:file_folder:)
liam: quick skim: tokens/sec delta v3_a vs v3_b shows v3_b (smaller batch clamp) wins for seq<=128. good signal.
maya: thumbs — schedule a 30m sync tomorrow to decide rollout. :thumbsup:
ben: ping me the report link and I'll add charts to the dashboard.
sophie: will also attach perf traces.
alex: I'll submit PRs for kv eviction and routing rule after the sync.
maya: thanks all. closing the thread after sync unless urgent regressions pop up. :white_check_mark:
